P8 validates uncertainty-aware online LOCA diagnosis on a 220 MWe pressurized heavy-water reactor, not a PWR; its transfer to PWR SB-LOCA remains a hypothesis.
P13 validates transfer learning on rotating-machine fault datasets, not reactor transient diagnosis; it is bridge evidence only.
P14 supports cross-condition/cross-facility transfer, but its simulation platform data were not verified as public in this run.

search_limitations: No configured Crossref/PubMed/arXiv academic-search MCP was callable; the Skill's OpenAlex fallback and official web/registry checks were used.
The search covered English-language public web and registry sources and is bounded, not exhaustive.
Direct ScienceDirect opens sometimes failed; exact official-domain results supplied publisher metadata and abstracts.
Only P7 is labeled fulltext_level, with named official-page section/equation anchors; every other selected record is abstract_level.
The 2026 articles are current as of the stated run date; no future publication state beyond the checked publisher/registry records is inferred.

No selected paper jointly demonstrates PWR SB-LOCA, explicit physics constraints, calibrated UQ, OOD detection, public data, and the exact resource budget. The proposed combination remains transfer-supported, not established.
NPPAD is public and physics-based, but a leak-safe SB-LOCA-only split and agreed early-warning horizon were not verified.
P20's physics-informed features are PWR-specific but not established for SB-LOCA, and its data accessibility is unverified.
P21 and P22 support UQ/OOD-style screening, but only P21's abstract mentions a public nuclear accident simulation platform; exact dataset identity and reusable splits remain unresolved.
No selected source reports training on the exact one-24-GB-GPU and 12-week budget; feasibility is plausible for the model families but unproven.
Primary endpoint, calibration metric, OOD composition, and acceptable false-alarm/detection-delay trade-off remain user decisions.

round_one_dispositions.reason: P25 is a newer direct PWR LOCA temporal study and better matches the added temporal-modeling preference.
Generic LOCA deep learning without current-round physics, UQ, or OOD evidence no longer fits the revised screening emphasis strongly enough for the six-paper default.
P21 directly contributes spatio-temporal Bayesian UQ and known/unknown-scenario evaluation, the newly requested screening dimensions.
Current official full text reconfirms the open PWR time-series anchor and explicit simulator physics needed under inherited data constraints.
Current publisher abstract reconfirms Bayesian confidence bounds for online LOCA diagnosis, directly supporting UQ screening with an explicit reactor-transfer caveat.
Its target evidence remains rotating-machine small-sample transfer and does not meet the new physics/UQ/OOD priority at target-domain strength.
P20 supplies explicit physics-based PWR feature augmentation, a closer bridge to the new physics-constrained preference than generic transfer learning.
P22 operationalizes uncertainty decomposition, domain discrepancy, and unknown-fault detection rather than treating them only as review-level concerns.

directions.title: Physics-constrained uncertainty-aware temporal SB-LOCA break-extent diagnosis

hard_gates.rationale: Eligible M1 records directly identify PWR LOCA diagnosis or prediction needs; the evidence does not by itself establish the proposed combined method.
P7 provides full-text-level support for an open PWR accident time-series dataset; a leak-safe SB-LOCA split remains a test-design unknown.
The bounded minimum decisive test specifies a held-out primary metric and numeric success, stop, and pivot thresholds.
One baseline and one bounded candidate fit the stated single-24-GB-GPU envelope by design; measured memory and wall time remain required outputs.
The decision test is limited to one fixed public-data split, one baseline, and one candidate, with a two-week cap inside the 12-week budget.
The test uses only public simulated data and is explicitly research-only, with no plant control, deployment, or safety claim.
Every cited ID resolves to a recommendation-eligible candidate in the accepted M1 round-two pool; basis-level limitations are retained.

concepts: Temporal PWR accident diagnosis can be paired with physics-derived features and predictive uncertainty only as a testable transfer hypothesis.
units: Simulator channel units and any derived conservation residuals must be normalized without erasing their physical definitions.
scales: Transient-window duration, sampling interval, and break-extent scale must be aligned before comparing baseline and candidate.
boundary_conditions: The evidence is bounded to simulated PWR/related nuclear scenarios and does not cover operational plant deployment.
assumptions: NPPAD contains enough labeled PWR LOCA trajectories to construct a non-leaking SB-LOCA-focused decision test.

anti_transfer_factors: P20 does not establish SB-LOCA-specific physics features.
P21 does not establish calibrated SB-LOCA uncertainty or the exact compute budget.
Simulator-to-plant and reactor-design shift can invalidate apparent gains.

dimensions.evidence: Full-text P7 anchors open simulated PWR data, while abstract-level P20, P21, P22, and P25 bound the physics, UQ/OOD, limitation, and direct-problem case. This engineering value score is a provisional comparison aid, not proof of target applicability.
unknowns: The exact early-warning horizon and primary operating trade-off are not user-confirmed.
change_triggers: Re-score if the bounded test, resource audit, or user-selected endpoint contradicts this assumption.

minimum_decisive_test.hypothesis: On one fixed held-out public SB-LOCA simulation split, adding physics-derived features and predictive uncertainty to a matched temporal baseline reduces break-extent error without exceeding the resource cap.
inputs: One frozen, public NPPAD/PCTRAN-PWR3LP SB-LOCA-focused split with train/validation/test trajectory separation
One matched temporal baseline and one physics-constrained uncertainty-aware candidate
minimum_decisive_test.baseline: The same temporal backbone without physics-derived features or predictive-uncertainty head, trained under the same fixed budget.
steps: Fit the baseline and candidate once under the same capped seed and epoch budget.
Evaluate the frozen held-out trajectories once and record error, calibration, peak GPU memory, and wall time.
minimum_decisive_test.primary_metric: relative reduction in held-out break-extent mean absolute error versus baseline
minimum_decisive_test.expected_time: At most 14 calendar days for the bounded comparison.
required_resources: One GPU with at most 24 GiB VRAM

unknowns: The operational early-warning horizon and preferred error/calibration trade-off are not user-confirmed.
A leak-safe SB-LOCA subset and split have not been established by M1.
No selected source establishes the combined method or its exact one-GPU cost.

axis_changes.to: mixed-accident NPPAD windows with held-out accident families

hard_gates.rationale: Eligible M1 records directly identify PWR LOCA diagnosis or prediction needs; the evidence does not by itself establish the proposed combined method.

concepts: Known/unknown nuclear-scenario uncertainty and open-set decisions may support early SB-LOCA triage, but this is a transfer hypothesis rather than established target performance.

minimum_decisive_test.hypothesis: On one fixed mixed-accident public simulation split with complete accident families held out, a Bayesian spatio-temporal classifier separates unknown from known scenarios while retaining SB-LOCA triage utility.
inputs: One frozen public mixed-accident NPPAD split with complete held-out accident families
One deterministic closed-set temporal baseline and one Bayesian open-set candidate
minimum_decisive_test.baseline: A deterministic closed-set temporal classifier with maximum-softmax unknown scoring on the identical split.
steps: Fit the baseline and one Bayesian open-set candidate under the same capped budget.
Evaluate once on known and completely held-out accident families and record AUROC, FPR95, SB-LOCA recall, memory, and time.
minimum_decisive_test.primary_metric: unknown-accident detection area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve

stop_condition.metric: false-positive rate at 95 percent true-positive rate

minimum_decisive_test.expected_time: At most 14 calendar days for the bounded comparison.
required_resources: One GPU with at most 24 GiB VRAM

unknowns: The operational cost of false unknown alarms is not user-confirmed.
A leakage-resistant held-out-accident protocol has not been established by M1.
The Bayesian/open-set combination and compute cost are not established for SB-LOCA.
